1 UNDER SECTION 173(1) OF M.V. ACT, PRAYING ALLOW THIS APPEAL BY SETTING ASIDE THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED 07.06.2016 PASSED BY THE II ADDL.
MACT AND ADDITIONAL DISTRICT JUDGE, BIDAR SITTING AT BHALKI IN MVC NO.613/2012 AND AWARD COMPENSATION AS CLAIMED IN THE CLAIM PETITION.

THIS MFA HAVING BEEN HEARD AND RESERVED FOR JUDGMENT ON 10.01.2023, COMING ON FOR PRONOUNCEMENT THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:-
 JUDGMENT
Not being satisfied with the quantum of compensation, petitioner has come up with this appeal under Section 173(1) of M.V.Act, seeking enhancement.
2. For the sake of convenience the parties are referred to by their rank before the Tribunal.
3. FACTS:
It is the case of the petitioner that on 23.10.2010, he was proceeding on his motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-39/H-6805 towards his land at Mogdal Village.

At about 7.30 a.m., near ice cream factory of one Meeraj, lorry bearing registration No.MH-25/U-2298 (hereinafter referred to as offending vehicle) came from his back side in a high speed, in rash or negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner.
Due to impact, petitioner sustained severe injuries.
Initially he was shifted to Mannaekhelli Hospital.
The concerned police recorded his statement and based on it registered a case in Cr.No.173/2010.
Later on he was shifted to Yashoda Hospital, Secunderabad.
He was treated as in-patient and has undergone prolonged treatment including surgery.
Despite treatment, he is not completely cured.
He has lost his memory and as such not able to work.
He has suffered 100% disability.
As the owner and insurer, respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
4. Though duly served respondent No.1 did not appear and as such he was placed ex-parte.

5. Respondent No.2 appeared and filed written statement denying the age, occupation, income,
nature of the injury sustained and that it has resulted in 100%.
There is violation of terms and conditions of the policy and as such respondent No.2 is not liable to pay the compensation.
6. Based on these pleadings, the Tribunal has framed necessary issues.
7. On behalf of petitioner, his wife is examined as PW-1 and another witness as PW-2.
Ex- P1 to 13 are marked.
8. Vide the impugned judgment and award the Tribunal has partly allowed the claim petition granting compensation in a sum of Rs.5,06,984/- with interest @ 6% p.a.

The details of compensation granted are as under:

. During the course of arguments learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that on account of the injury sustained by the petitioner, there is 100% disability and as such petitioner is unable to work as he used to.
Therefore, the compensation granted under the head loss of future income is on the lower side.
The income of the petitioner taken at Rs.6,000/- per month by the Tribunal is on the lower side.
The compensation granted under the remaining heads is also on the lower side and requires reconsideration.

10. On the other hand learned counsel for respondent No.2 supported the impugned judgment and award and submitted that the petitioner has failed to establish that he has suffered 100% disability and having regard to the evidence placed on record, the age of the petitioner, the compensation granted is on the higher side and prays to dismiss the appeal.

11. Heard arguments and perused the record.
12.

In the light of the specific grounds urged in the appeal, it is necessary to examine whether the compensation granted to the petitioner under the various heads is just and reasonable or it calls for any interference.
13. At the outset, it is relevant to note that the petitioner has not stepped into the witness box.

On the other hand he has examined his wife as his guardian on the ground that he has suffered 100%
disability.

If at all the disability suffered by the petitioner is 100% or such that he is not in a position to give evidence, the least the petitioner could have done was to present himself before the Court and enable the Court to examine him, at least superficially to ascertain whether he is able to understand questions put by the Court and give logical answer.
Admittedly, neither petitioner nor his wife who is stated to be his guardian has done so.
Thereby, petitioner has lost an opportunity to demonstrate that after the accident, he is not a normal person and not in a position to give logical answer due to head injury suffered by him.
14. Petitioner has examined Dr.B.J.Rajesh of Yashoda Hospital, Secunderabad as PW-2.

It is pertinent to note that during the course of his evidence, this witness has not stated his specialty,
whether he is a Neuro surgeon or in what faculty he is working.
In Ex.P.5, which is discharge summary, this witness i.e., Dr.B.J. Rajesh is shown as consultant Neurosurgeon.

He has also not Dr.Syed Mahboob Ali S/O Syed Ali vs Naredra S/O Gurulingappa Patil And Anr on 17 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147635413/
3 deposed that the petitioner was under his treatment.

sentences.text: He has generally deposed regarding the treatment given.

He has only stated that petitioner is suffering from mood fluctuation, memory loss,
giddiness and lethargy and that due to his neurological status, he needs regular follow-up treatment.
PW-2 has issued certificate as per Ex.P12 stating that petitioner remains to have Neuro psychological disability.
However, he has not produced detailed examination in the requisite proforma on the basis of which he has come to such a conclusion.

During his cross-examination,
PW-2 has stated that petitioner was referred to clinical psychologist for Neuro psychological assessment on 13.09.2013, but the report by the clinical psychologist is not produced/present.

15. Ex.P.12 is a certificate dated 24.10.2013 issued by P.W.2 stating that petitioner remains to have Neuro psychological disabilities due to head injury, including moderate cognitive impairment,
reduced memory and late post traumatic seizure.
On the other hand, Ex.P.8 is a certificate issued by the RMO of Yashoda hospital stating that the injuries suffered by the petitioner and that he has been advised not to work.
In the absence of detailed report of clinical psychologist for neuro psychological assessment, no reliance could be placed on Exs.P.8 and 12 to hold that the petitioner has suffered 100% disability.

16. The examination of the documents produced by the petitioner in the light of evidence of PW-2 makes it evident that the contention of the petitioner that he has suffered 100% disability cannot be accepted.
Consequently, taking all these aspects into consideration, the Tribunal has rightly calculated the disability of petitioner at 40% and it requires no reconsideration.

17. Even though the petitioner has claimed that he was Registered Medical Practitioner (RMP) and earning Rs.10,000/- p.m., he has not produced any document to show that he was a Registered Medical Practitioner and his income was Rs.10,000/-p.m.

Since the accident occurred during 2010,
based on minimum wages the income of the petitioner ought to have been taken at Rs.5,500/-.
The Tribunal has taken it at Rs.6,000/-p.m and therefore there is no need to interfere with the same.
18. Though the petitioner has claimed that he was aged 55 years at the time of accident, the medical records state that he was aged around 59-60 years.
For the age group of 56-60 years, the Tribunal has correctly taken the multiplier as 9.
With these components, it is necessary to examine whether compensation granted under the following various heads is just and reasonable or whether it requires any enhancement.
19. Pain and suffering & Loss of amenities of life:

As per Ex.P8, petitioner has suffered right fronto temporal contusion, left temporo parietal delayed contusion with bi-parietal SAH and chest injury - fracture of right 7, 8 and 9 ribs and also left 5, 6 ribs.

Having regard to the fact that the accident is of the year 2010 and taking into consideration the nature of injury suffered, grant of compensation in a sum of Rs.40,000/- under the head pain and suffering is just and proper.
However, compensation in a sum of Rs.10,000/- granted under the head loss of amenities of life is on the lower side.

The same is enhanced to Rs.20,000/-.
20.
Medical expenses:
Based on the medical bills produced by the petitioner, the Tribunal has rightly granted compensation in a sum of Rs.1,87,784/- and it requires no modification.

4 21. Conveyance and nourishment:

The Tribunal has granted compensation in a sum of Rs.10,000/-
under this head.

Having regard to fact that petitioner has taken treatment at Yashodha Hospital,
Secunderabad and has also undergone surgery, the compensation under this head is enhanced to Rs.20,000/-.
22. Loss of future earning:
Taking into consideration the income at Rs.6,000/- and disability at 40%, the Tribunal has granted compensation in a sum of Rs.2,59,200/- under this head.

However,
while calculating the same, the Tribunal has not included loss of future prospects.

As per the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd vs Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram & Ors1, having regard to the age of the petitioner, 10% of his income is required to be added towards loss of future prospects.

sentences.text: Since his income is taken at Rs.6,000/- p.m., 10% of it works out to be Rs.600/-.
Therefore, the income of the petitioner is required to be taken as Rs.6,600/-.
With the multiplier 9 and disability at 40%, compensation under the head loss of future earnings comes to Rs.6,600 x 12 x 9 x 40% = Rs.2,85,120/- as against Rs.2,59,200/- granted by the Tribunal.

Thus, in all petitioner is entitled for total compensation in a sum of (2018) 18 SCC 130 Rs.5,52,904/- as against Rs.5,06,984/- granted by the Tribunal as detailed below:

 ORDER  (i) Appeal is allowed in part.
 (ii) Appellant/petitioner is entitled for compensation in a sum of Rs.5,52,904/- as against Rs.5,06,984/- granted by the Tribunal, with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till realization.
